analysis.title: GS Dunn - GS US Daily Download 21 Oct 2026
key_insights: 16% of the S&P 500 reports earnings this week, and over half the index will have reported by month-end.

GS's US consumer dashboard shows weak income growth and weak consumer confidence but otherwise healthy consumer fundamentals. Real PCE growth is 2.6% y/y and 3.9% annualised over 6 months, so GS is less concerned about a meaningful consumption slowdown despite higher energy prices.

GS expects real disposable income growth to slow to 1.2% in 2026 and recover to 2.1% in 2027 as inflation falls. Underlying job growth is around breakeven, unemployment is 4.2%, and GS expects about 55k/month job growth through 2027.

Household balance sheets are very strong. Net worth relative to disposable income is near all-time highs and the saving rate is stable around 4.1%. GS concludes this argues against a significant consumer downturn.

Netflix Q3 came in above Street and GS estimates with a slightly below-consensus Q4 guide that GS thinks may prove conservative. Management says the long-term growth algorithm of member growth, pricing and advertising is intact, supporting double-digit revenue growth.
Netflix management is refocusing on US and Canada content success and engagement. GS sees this as the key investor debate for the stock from current levels.

Netflix 2026 advertising revenue will likely come in below prior forecast, citing ad product timelines and third-party integration of ad products and measurement. GS still believes advertising is underappreciated and under-modelled over a multi-year view.
Netflix content investment is focused on scaling live content, licensing and third-party content aggregation, which GS calls evolution rather than revolution. Most spend remains on original content.
GE Aerospace Q3 results beat GS's model and FactSet consensus across the board, and several components of the 2026 outlook were raised. GS raised estimates again and rates the stock Buy.
GE Aerospace drivers: strong aftermarket fundamentals, heightened order activity, an improving new engine ramp, solid defence demand, pricing power, cost performance and high cash conversion.
Natural gas E&P sentiment is mixed despite +8% 3-month performance in GS coverage. Strong Permian associated gas supply growth and weaker winter demand from El Niño are the concerns.
3Q26 revisions are trending down across GS's gas E&P coverage because Appalachian Basin differentials widened in September. GS sees possible upside to curtailed volumes in the region.

GS reiterates a mid-cycle Henry Hub price of $3.50/MMBtu for 2027/2028. It highlights AR (13% FCF yield on average 2027/2028 estimates), EQT (low-cost integrated Appalachian producer with power and LNG demand momentum) and EXE (12% FCF yield on average 2027/2028 estimates).

Market update: equities stabilised after a shaky start driven by overnight global tech weakness (KOSPI -40%, a $150mn Korean neocloud IPO finished -32%). RTY outperformed SPX, which outperformed NDX. The rally felt squeezy with short pockets leading, and about 400 S&P names finished up.

Desk flow was not convincing. Floor activity was 4 out of 10 and finished +3% better to buy on muted notional. Info Tech volumes were -15% vs the 10-day average, the desk was a net seller of Semis/AI into the bounce at a slower pace than the prior week, and ETFs were 32% of the tape.

Post-bell moves: SPCX +1.5% on a headline revenue/EBITDA beat (market likely sees a beat vs consensus but soft vs whisper), NFLX -5% retesting its YTD low after lowering the FY ad revenue outlook, UAL -1.7%, COF +5% on a beat, ISRG -11% on a modest procedure beat against heightened expectations.
UAL Q3 EPS was $2.54 vs $2.57 expected on $17.9bn revenue in line with consensus. Q4 guide is well below at $0.50-1.50 vs $1.88 expected, with $4.80 jet fuel expected in Q4.

market_movers.rationale: GE Aerospace Q3 results beat GS and FactSet consensus, 2026 outlook components were raised, and GS raised estimates again. Strong aftermarket, orders and cash conversion.
Highlighted for its structural cost reduction pathway and a 13% FCF yield on average 2027/2028 estimates.
Low-cost integrated Appalachian producer benefiting from operating efficiencies and commercial momentum with power and LNG end markets.
Durable cash flow profile, a commercial strategy focus and a 12% FCF yield on average 2027/2028 estimates.
Q3 was above Street and GS, Q4 guide slightly below, and 2026 ad revenue is below prior forecast. GS still sees advertising as underappreciated and under-modelled.

sector_views.rationale: Investor sentiment is mixed on Permian associated gas growth and El Niño demand risk. GS screens the group for risk/reward skew and valuation, with a $3.50/MMBtu mid-cycle Henry Hub view.
GE Aerospace shows strong aftermarket, orders, defence demand and pricing power.
Spending is resilient and balance sheets are strong, though income growth and confidence are weak and energy prices are higher.

earnings_insights: Netflix Q3 reported 10/20: above Street and GS estimates (no figures given). Q4 guide slightly below Street/GS (guide, no figures given). 2026 ad revenue outlook lowered. The stock fell about 5% post-bell and retested its YTD low.
GE Aerospace Q3 reported: ahead of GS model and FactSet consensus across the board. Several components of the 2026 outlook were revised higher.
United Airlines Q3 reported 10/20: EPS $2.54 vs $2.57 consensus, revenue $17.9bn in line with consensus. Q4 EPS guide $0.50-1.50 vs $1.88 consensus, assuming $4.80 jet fuel.
Capital One reported a beat and rose about 5% post-bell (no figures given).
Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) reported a modest procedure beat against heightened expectations, pointing to the midpoint of the tightened guidance range. The stock fell about 11% post-bell.

SpaceX (SPCX) reported a headline revenue/EBITDA beat. The stock rose 1.5% post-bell and the call at 4:30pm ET focused on GW deployment, data center leasing and Starlink direct-to-mobile. Market likely sees a beat vs consensus but soft vs whisper.
Upcoming 10/21 pre-market earnings: PM, TMO, ABT, NEE, T, DHR, CME, ELV, MCO, WAB. Post-market: META, TSLA, LRCX, SAP, TXN, IBM, CSX, KMI, URI, WCN.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Spending is holding up despite higher energy prices, lowering the odds of a consumption slowdown.
Employment appears stabilised, with underlying job growth around breakeven.
Broadly stable and supported by strong household balance sheets.
Income growth slows this year and recovers as inflation falls.
Modest job growth consistent with a stabilised labour market.
GS's mid-cycle price view underpins its gas E&P valuations.

risk_factors: Weak income growth and weak consumer confidence in the US consumer dashboard.
Higher energy prices weighing on consumers, and $4.80 jet fuel in Q4 for airlines.
Permian associated gas supply growth and El Niño-driven weaker winter demand for natural gas producers.
Global tech weakness (KOSPI -40%, a Korean neocloud IPO -32%) hitting sentiment at the open.
Netflix US content performance and ad product execution.
